title: Decision sentiment biomarker for model substitution
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Objective: define and validate a compact set of correlated signals (a 'decision sentiment biomarker') that predicts when customers and internal stakeholders will accept a model substitution or require human-in-the-loop (HITL) remediation. This ticket scopes a lightweight research + instrumentation spike to: 1) identify behavioral and telemetry signals that indicate substitution acceptance friction, 2) prototype a scoring function that maps signals to a substitution risk score, and 3) validate the score against historical switch decisions and two field probes. Outcome should inform automated fallback routing thresholds and procurement/negotiation playbooks.
background: We see repeated enterprise churn risk during forced model substitutions (supply outage, deprecation, or cost-driven variant switches). Current heuristics (latency/cost buckets) miss adoption sentiment: customers sometimes tolerate higher latency for perceived accuracy or regulatory provenance. We need a reproducible signal set that combines product telemetry, billing, support interactions, and sales/procurement notes to estimate substitution acceptance probability.
acceptance_criteria: Documented candidate signals (>=10) across telemetry, support, and commercial signals with rationale
A prototype scoring function implemented as a notebook + scoring lambda that outputs a normalized 0-100 substitution acceptance score
Backtest of the score against at least 120 historical substitution attempts with precision/recall and AUC reported
Two field probes (canary with 50 customers total): one benign low-cost substitution and one price-driven quantized fallback, with pre/post NPS and usage delta tracked
Runbook notes for using the score in automated routing (thresholds and recommended human escalation paths)
